questions.q: What is the Databricks sidebar's "Compute" section for?
options: Creating and managing clusters
Scheduling recurring notebook runs
Browsing and organizing notebooks and files
Unity Catalog governance over tables and schemas
questions.explain: This is covered in depth in Lesson 4.

questions.q: What's the difference between the Home folder and the Shared folder?
options: They are functionally identical with no real difference
Home is your personal, private-by-default folder; Shared is visible to everyone in the workspace
Shared is only accessible to workspace admins, never regular users
Home is for notebooks, Shared is only for raw data files
questions.explain: Shared is the natural home for anything a team works on together.

questions.q: What does the "Catalog" section of the sidebar relate to?
options: Scheduling Lakeflow pipeline runs
A list of all notebooks ever created in the workspace
Pricing tiers available for the workspace
Unity Catalog — catalogs, schemas, and tables, covered in this course's Chapter 4
questions.explain: This is where governance over every table created from Chapter 2 onward eventually gets managed.

questions.q: Why might a team convention favor saving reusable notebooks in Shared rather than Home?
options: Home folders are deleted automatically after 24 hours
Defaulting everything to a personal Home folder means nobody else on the team can find or reuse it
There's no real difference; it's purely a matter of preference with no practical impact
Notebooks saved in Home cannot be attached to a cluster
questions.explain: This mirrors the same instinct behind Foundations' raw/cleansed data-zone separation, applied to code instead of data.

questions.q: Where do notebooks actually live in Databricks?
options: They exist only in memory and disappear when a cluster stops
Notebooks are stored separately from any file browser, with no visible location
They can only be stored inside a Unity Catalog volume
As regular files in the Workspace file browser, organized in folders just like any other file system
questions.explain: Nothing about notebook storage is exotic — it's browsable and organizable like any folder structure.
